newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One asks for listing extension.
newsitem.headline: Finance One asks for listing extension.

text.p: Ailing Thai finance and securities company Finance One Plc has requested an extension in listing of recently-issued new shares, the company said in a statement on Friday.

"Finance One reported it could not apply for listing of its 611,938 new common shares within 30 days from the subscription date by July 24 1997 and has requested the Stock Exchange of Thailand for an extension," the statement said.
The new shares are those subscribed to by existing shareholders during a 827.24 million new share rights issue.
The firm has offered unsubscribed shares to the central bank's Financial Institutions Development Fund. The fund has not yet agreed to buy the new shares, the statement said.
The troubled firm, which lost 5.23 billion baht ($163 million) during the first half of 1997, was the largest of 16 troubled finance companies suspended from operations by the central bank in June.
